about: Every key of the 16 vendor Telugu keyboards (C:/Shree-Lipi nxt/*.TEL, loaded from their original paths) answered by S8TelU64.dll (TutorGetMappedCodeW, Unicode) and S8Tel764.dll (TutorGetMappedCode, Shree-Lipi 7 raw bytes; the 4/5/6 fonts SHREE-TEL-* draw the same bytes with the same glyphs). Two capture runs (capvo/, capvo-b/) were identical (after normalising the random unit count the 7 composer returns for "no answer"), and each run asked every key twice (#stable 1); every load verified in SLNXT's shared table (#loaded 1). layer 0 = printed keyboard (normal and shift are different ASCII keys), layer 1 = Ctrl+Space, layer 2 = the composer raw code layer (key char = internal code; NOT the Ctrl+Shift+1 symbol layer, which the tutor does not expose - see ctrlShift1). Per key: codes = the internal codes the key holds (a conjunct slot expanded, typed order), uHex/u = the Unicode composer answer raw / without its carrier, uRead = u with the ra-vattu "*్ర" read as ్ర on its cluster, b7 = the 7 composer bytes. u null = no answer or a placeholder ("Lk" = the link code 64 alone). b7 "E6 61 E6 61" = the 7 composer's answer for a lone vowel sign (a carrier, not a spelling).

o.b7: AB A7 E6 FE 79 E6 FE

ctrlShift1.source: the vendor charts (CHM "Special Keys", the same 16 keys in all 18 Telugu charts: assets/config/layouts/tel-*.json and telugu-inscript.json "symbols") + the composers' answers for the internal code of each character (single-code probes, capp/P-results.json). b7 null = the 7 composer types nothing for that code.
